title: Gerber, CA on I-5: Exit 642 Guide
meta: Gerber sits at exit 642 on I-5 in Tehama County: a railroad division point from 1916 to 1965, with rest areas 7.6 miles south and 14.2 miles north.
intro: Gerber is a Tehama County stop on I-5 reached at exit 642 (Proberta, Gerber, Flores Avenue). East of the freeway, the town was platted in 1910 and served as a Southern Pacific Railroad division point from 1916 to 1965. This is the northern end of a band of farmland that runs almost unbroken to Bakersfield.

faq.q: What exit is Gerber on I-5?
faq.a: Gerber is at exit 642 on I-5, signed as Proberta, Gerber, Flores Avenue. The town itself lies east of the freeway.

faq.q: What is the history of Gerber, California?
faq.a: Gerber was platted in 1910 and named for the Gerber family, who owned the town site. From 1916 to 1965 it was a Southern Pacific Railroad division point where steam locomotives took on fuel, got repairs and changed crews.

faq.q: Where is the nearest rest area to Gerber on I-5?
faq.a: The Lt. John C. Helmick Rest Area is 7.6 miles south, and the Herbert S. Miles Rest Area is 14.2 miles north. Both serve traffic in both directions.

faq.q: Which towns are before and after Gerber on I-5?
faq.a: Heading north, Tehama is the next town to the south and Red Bluff is the next town to the north.
